subject: Discovery recap - observability & evals (dashboards, tracing hooks, golden prompts)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan@zenhealth.com>, Tara Wilson <t.wilson@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap - observability & evals (ZenHealth)

Hi Jordan / Tara - thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: late detection of model quality regressions and poor per-route observability (takes days to detect production drift).
- Goal: detect regressions within hours, get per-route diagnostics, and have automated regression alerts + rollout guardrails for safe canaries.

What we heard on the call
- Pain points:
  1) No unified observability across inference endpoints; logs are fragmented between app and model infra.
  2) Regressions discovered by users or CS tickets - mean time to detect is multiple days.
  3) Difficulty reproducing MLOps regressions because there are no golden prompt sets or stable eval harnesses.
  4) Need for tracing hooks to correlate request traces with token-level errors and latency spikes.

- Current stack:
  * Inference: homegrown endpoints + a mix of hosted backends for burst capacity
  * Logging: central ELK for app logs, separate metrics for infra
  * CI: automated model training but limited post-deploy evals

- Success criteria (what ZenHealth will call a win):
  * Time-to-detect regressions < 4 hours for priority routes
  * Per-route dashboards with quality + latency + cost breakdowns
  * Regression alerts that trigger a rollback or canary pause when quality drops > X%
  * Ability to run scheduled evals against a golden prompt set and see trend graphs

Requested observability + evals features we discussed
- Per-route dashboards (top 10 user flows) with token-level latency, 95/99 latency percentiles, and quality metrics.
- Tracing hooks that surface example inputs/outputs and KV cache state for failing requests.
- Golden prompt sets (we proposed templated XLSX) and a baseline eval harness for A/B and regression testing.
- Regression alerts and automated rollout guardrails (canary thresholds, automatic fallback to previous model if quality drops).

Attachments & links
- Attached: zenhealth-observability-primer.pdf (sample dashboards + recommended metrics)
- Attached: golden-prompt-sets.xlsx (template for collecting golden prompts)
- Drive preview link: https://drive.google.com/zenhealth/obs-dashboards-sample

Next steps
1) I will send the primer + golden prompt template (attached). [Action: Marissa - sent]
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your engineering + platform team to map tracing hooks and dashboard requirements (2 weeks). [Action: Jordan/Tara - propose 2-3 times]
3) Share a short mutual-action-plan outlining milestones for a 6-week eval (SLOs, dashboards, rollout guardrails). [Action: Marissa - will draft by Mon 6/29]

If that all looks right I can get the technical agenda ready and include our runtime engineer for the tracing discussion.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: zenhealth-observability-primer.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: golden-prompt-sets.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)]

From: Jordan Smith <jordan@zenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - observability & evals (ZenHealth)

Thanks Marissa - this is great and accurate. A few clarifications / additions from our side:

1) Priority routes: patient intake and clinical summary generation are highest priority - these are where we've seen the most user-facing regressions.
2) Thresholds: for regressions we'd like to start with a 5% drop in our quality metric (F1/ROUGE proxy) as an initial canary threshold.
3) Team for deep-dive: I'll bring in our platform lead, Tara Wilson (cc'd), and our ML infra engineer, Sam Patel (sam@zenhealth.com).

For scheduling - we're available next Wed (7/1) or Thu (7/2) morning PST. Can you confirm availability and whether we should include any of your runtime engineers?

Also: we'll upload an initial set of ~120 golden prompts to the template you attached and share before the deep-dive.

Thanks - excited to move forward.

Jordan
Head of Product, ZenHealth
jordan@zenhealth.com

I'll also prepare a short mutual-action-plan doc and a preliminary SLO proposal to share ahead of the meeting.

Thanks - Marissa
